answer: Escrowed Operator Liability. Each identity's on-chain actions are signed through a per-operator kernel that accumulates unresolved disputes. When an identity is caught in a sybil cluster, the penalty debits the operator's escrow account across all their identities, not just the offending wallet, pushing the operator toward a liability nadir where further operations become unprofitable. A hollow shell wallet with no escrow cannot transact, so farming identities requires funding fresh escrow per cluster, multiplying attacker cost linearly with each duplicate.
